title: Write Insertion Sort
statement:
Implement **insertion sort**. You are given an array of `n` integers. Sort it in non-decreasing order and print the sorted array.

Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix one element at a time. For each index `i` from `1` to `n - 1`, take `arr[i]` as the key, shift every larger element of the sorted prefix `arr[0..i-1]` one position to the right, and drop the key into the gap that opens up.

Equal elements keep their original relative order (the sort is stable), though with plain integers this is not visible in the output.

**Follow-up:** explain why insertion sort runs in `O(n)` time on an already sorted array, and why it is a good choice for small or nearly sorted inputs.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the `n` integers in non-decreasing order, separated by single spaces.

examples.explanation: After i=1: 3 9 7 1 4. After i=2: 3 7 9 1 4. After i=3: 1 3 7 9 4. After i=4: 1 3 4 7 9.
The key -1 is shifted past both 2s at the front. The final array is -1 2 2 2.

hints: Keep the prefix arr[0..i-1] sorted at all times; the loop invariant is what makes the algorithm correct.
Save arr[i] in a variable, then walk j leftwards while arr[j] is greater than the key, copying arr[j] to arr[j + 1].
When the walk stops, write the key at position j + 1.
